global.headline: TRUMP BRANDS IRAN 'DUPLICITOUS' AS TEHRAN DENIES DIRECT TALKS, OIL EXTENDS ITS SLIDE, AND ISRAEL DEFIES PRESSURE TO HALT GAZA STRIKES
summary: President Trump said Monday that renewed talks with Iran are Tehran's "last chance" to sign a deal reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending its nuclear ambitions, insisting from the Oval Office that he faces no time pressure since he is not seeking re-election. But the day turned contentious after Iran's foreign ministry said Tehran was holding no direct talks with the United States at all — only with Oman, over a "temporary" shipping route through the strait that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said was in its "final stage." Trump responded on social media by branding the Iranian regime "extremely duplicitous," saying officials had asked for talks only to then deny any were taking place, and reiterating that negotiations would proceed in two phases: reopening the strait first, denuclearisation second. No signed agreement exists; Saturday's cancellation of a planned joint US-Israel strike remains only a mutual pause built on a stated outline.

Oil extended Sunday's sharp reversal: Brent crude fell a further roughly 4.7% to about $83.81 a barrel Monday, unwinding more of July's near-25% run-up, as traders read the Oman-Hormuz progress — even absent a US-Iran deal — as the more market-moving signal than the unresolved diplomatic spat over who exactly is negotiating with whom.

The pause has not extended to Gaza. Nikolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza, held what officials called "constructive and detailed" talks with Prime Minister Netanyahu on Monday and separately pressed him to halt Israeli strikes while the group's 15-point Hamas disarmament deal is implemented. Israel instead struck Gaza for the first time in a day, killing a man the military identified as Jalal Sobieh, a commander in Hamas's Daraj-Tuffah Battalion, and said both this and an earlier strike targeted operatives "advancing attacks" on troops and civilians. Israeli officials also confirmed they had conveyed "serious security concerns" about the disarmament deal's published terms directly to Washington, with Netanyahu's spokesman saying the public version "does not reflect Israel's positions" — a rift that, together with the weekend's Gaza toll of at least 26 dead, underscores how narrow the Iran-specific de-escalation actually is.
global.geopolitical: A Trump administration that spent Saturday claiming credit for cancelling an imminent joint strike on Iran spent Monday publicly accusing Tehran of bad faith — a whiplash that exposes how thin the current pause is: it rests on informal Oman-mediated shipping-route talks rather than any US-Iran channel, while Israel's parallel disavowal of the Hamas disarmament deal's public terms shows Washington's two most consequential Middle East tracks are both running on unresolved daylight between the US and its own partners rather than settled agreements with adversaries.
global.socioeconomic: A second consecutive double-digit-percentage slide in Brent crude — now roughly 20 percentage points off its recent peak in two trading sessions — shows markets pricing the Hormuz-specific thaw as durable even as the broader war's other fronts (Gaza, and the still-unresolved US-Iran channel itself) remain unresolved, a divergence that will leave fuel-dependent economies exposed to a rapid reversal if either track collapses.

global.headline: SUDANESE ARMY DRONE STRIKE ON DARFUR CUSTOMARY COURT KILLS AT LEAST 35
summary: A Sudanese army drone strike hit a customary court session held under a tree in Ghara al-Zawiya, a village in North Darfur controlled by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, killing at least 35 people and wounding dozens more, according to the Emergency Lawyers Group, a rights monitor tracking civilian harm in Sudan's civil war. The court was hearing local land and community disputes with tribal leaders present when the strike hit at around 1pm local time Sunday; the dead included four tribal leaders and two RSF commanders. Sudan's army, which has been fighting the RSF for control of the country since April 2023, has not commented on the strike.
global.geopolitical: Striking a civilian dispute-resolution gathering rather than a military target deepens international concern that Sudan's army, like the RSF it is fighting, is willing to inflict mass civilian casualties in Darfur with near-total impunity, in a war that has drawn far less sustained international mediation pressure than conflicts of comparable scale elsewhere.
global.socioeconomic: The loss of tribal leaders who mediate land and resource disputes strips Darfur's already-fractured communities of one of the few remaining local mechanisms for resolving conflict without violence, compounding a humanitarian crisis in which famine conditions and mass displacement were already stretching aid access to breaking point.

global.headline: UKRAINIAN DRONE HITS CROWDED RUSSIAN BLACK SEA BEACH, KILLING SEVEN INCLUDING THREE CHILDREN
summary: At least seven people, including three children, were killed and around 40 injured Monday when a drone struck the beach resort area of Arkhipo-Osipovka, near Gelendzhik on Russia's Black Sea coast, regional governor Veniamin Kondratiev said. It remains unclear whether the drone was shot down by Russian air defences before crashing or hit the crowded beach directly. Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused Ukraine of "terrorism" and claimed NATO and EU countries were directly implicated in the strike; there was no immediate comment from Kyiv, which — like Moscow — says it does not deliberately target civilians in the war now in its fifth year.
global.geopolitical: A civilian death toll at a resort beach, regardless of whether the drone was intercepted or struck directly, hands Moscow a propaganda opening to frame Ukraine's deep-strike campaign as indiscriminate at a moment when Kyiv is simultaneously trying to demonstrate that campaign's military precision against refineries and airfields, complicating Ukraine's narrative with Western backers.
global.socioeconomic: Recurring strikes near Russian civilian infrastructure and tourist areas add to a mutually escalating pattern — Russia's own campaign against Ukrainian fuel stations runs in parallel — in which both countries' energy and leisure economies absorb rising costs and safety risks the longer the war continues without a negotiated de-escalation.

global.headline: FIRST DEATHS REPORTED IN US CYCLOSPORA OUTBREAK AS MICHIGAN CASE COUNT TOPS 11,000
summary: Michigan health officials reported the first two US deaths linked to the ongoing cyclosporiasis outbreak traced to recalled Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce, the CDC confirmed Monday, saying both individuals had significant underlying health conditions that dehydration and infection may have worsened. Michigan alone has recorded 11,234 cases and 193 hospitalisations; the CDC has logged more than 6,700 laboratory-confirmed cases nationally since 1 May, and the recall — covering bagged salads sold in grocery stores and served at chains including Taco Bell — now spans 27 US states. The CDC describes cyclosporiasis as rarely fatal, underscoring how unusual the deaths are relative to the outbreak's scale.
global.geopolitical: The outbreak's spread across more than half of US states via a single recalled-produce supply chain renews scrutiny of the fragmented, largely voluntary US food-safety recall system, a recurring point of friction between public-health regulators seeking mandatory standards and an agriculture industry resistant to tighter federal oversight.
global.socioeconomic: With cases surpassing 11,000 in Michigan alone and the first confirmed deaths now on record, the largest recorded Cyclospora outbreak in US history is starting to impose real costs beyond individual illness — hospital capacity strain, lost recalled-produce revenue for growers and retailers, and renewed consumer wariness toward pre-bagged salad greens generally.

global.headline: VON DER LEYEN CALLS FOR REINFORCED EU BORDERS AND MORE SUPPORT FOR MOROCCO AFTER CEUTA CROSSING
summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote to Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez on Monday proposing the EU further reinforce physical barriers and border-management systems at "critical points" and increase technical and financial support to Morocco, to prevent a repeat of last week's roughly 60,000-person crossing into Ceuta — the largest such border surge ever recorded in Europe over so short a period. The letter, ahead of Tuesday's Justice and Home Affairs Council convened by Ireland's EU presidency, marks von der Leyen's first substantive policy response beyond confirming the emergency meeting, coming after Spain publicly rebuked Italy and Denmark's push for the talks as "selfish, polarising and unlawful."
global.geopolitical: Proposing enhanced physical barriers and stepped-up support to Morocco — rather than a redistribution mechanism among EU members — signals the Commission is leaning toward externalising border control further rather than resolving the intra-EU political rift Spain's rebuke of Italy and Denmark exposed, a choice likely to satisfy migration hawks more than states bearing the humanitarian load.
global.socioeconomic: Deeper EU financial support for Moroccan border enforcement would formalise a dependency already central to Spain's migration strategy, but does nothing for the exhausted holdouts still sheltering on Ceuta's streets and beaches, leaving the territory's already-strained local services to absorb the crisis's human cost in the interim.

singapore.headline: 23-YEAR-OLD WORKER KILLED AS SCAFFOLDING COLLAPSES ONTO LORRY AT JURONG PORT WORKSITE
summary: A 23-year-old worker died Monday morning after scaffolding collapsed onto the lorry he was driving at a construction worksite along Jurong Port Road. SCDF and police were alerted at about 9.50am and found him trapped in the driver's seat; he was pronounced dead at the scene. Photos of the aftermath showed the collapsed structure lying across the site. The cause of the collapse is under investigation.
singapore.geopolitical: The death adds to a run of fatal Singapore worksite accidents this year that has repeatedly drawn attention to enforcement gaps in a construction sector still heavily reliant on migrant labour, a workforce-safety pattern regional labour-rights groups have flagged as a recurring cross-border concern.
singapore.socioeconomic: Coming after Q1's retrenchment spike and a construction sector already absorbing cost pressures from tariffs and materials inflation, another fatal workplace accident sharpens scrutiny of whether safety compliance is being squeezed alongside margins on major infrastructure and port-related projects.

singapore.headline: FIVE TRAPPED, THREE UNCONSCIOUS AS FIRE ENGULFS FARRER PARK FLAT
summary: SCDF was alerted to a fire in a fifth-floor unit at Block 684 Race Course Road, Farrer Park, at about 7.10pm Monday. Firefighters found five people trapped inside; one was rescued by police before SCDF's arrival. All five, three of whom had fallen unconscious, were taken to hospital — three to Singapore General Hospital and two to Tan Tock Seng Hospital. The fire, which started in a bedroom, is under investigation; no cause has yet been determined.
singapore.geopolitical: A second serious HDB fire within days of the Clementi blaze whose dry-riser equipment failure was disclosed just Sunday keeps residential fire-safety readiness under active public scrutiny, even though this incident has not yet raised the same equipment-failure questions.
singapore.socioeconomic: Repeated fire incidents with multiple casualties in older housing stock renew pressure on town councils and HDB to accelerate fire-safety equipment audits, an inspection and maintenance cost that ultimately flows through to residents via conservancy charges.

singapore.headline: MAN GETS 21 YEARS' JAIL, CANING FOR SEXUALLY ABUSING NIECE, 13, OVER TWO YEARS
summary: A 38-year-old man was sentenced Monday to 21 years' jail and 16 strokes of the cane after pleading guilty to six charges, including statutory rape and sexual assault, for abusing his niece over nearly two years starting when she was 13. The court heard the abuse began after he took her out on her birthday, that he raped her during staycations, and that he used sex acts to "punish" her when he grew jealous over a schoolmate she was dating. A further 17 charges were taken into consideration for sentencing. The man's identity has not been disclosed to protect the victim.
singapore.geopolitical: The sentence sits within a well-established Singapore sentencing framework for intra-family child sexual abuse, which courts have continued to treat as an aggravated breach of trust warranting lengthy jail terms and corporal punishment regardless of the absence of any external or online-recruitment element.
singapore.socioeconomic: Cases like this one, alongside the exploitation-ring charges filed in court a day earlier, keep pressure on family-service and school-based safeguarding programmes to catch abuse occurring inside trusted family relationships, which remains harder to detect than online-enabled exploitation by strangers.

singapore.headline: SINGAPORE'S CHAN CHUN SING WARNS ASEAN AGAINST 'DATA PROTECTIONISM' AT REGIONAL FORUM
summary: Speaking at the 18th ASEAN and Asia Forum, organised by the Singapore Institute of International Affairs, Defence Minister Chan Chun Sing called on ASEAN member states to deepen cooperation on data sharing, energy and finance to unlock new sources of regional growth. Data, he said, is "the new lubricant for the future economy" — unlike oil, a depletable resource, data can be shared without being consumed — and warned that "data protectionism" risks holding back the seamless cross-border data flows that increasingly underpin growth sectors across the region.
singapore.geopolitical: Framing data-sharing as ASEAN's next growth lever, delivered by Singapore's defence minister at a forum explicitly covering the region's positioning amid US-China strategic competition, signals Singapore continuing to position itself as an advocate for ASEAN economic integration as a hedge against major-power bloc formation around competing data and technology standards.
singapore.socioeconomic: A push toward looser cross-border data flows would particularly benefit Singapore's own data-centre, cloud and financial-services sectors, which depend on regional data mobility, even as individual ASEAN members weigh those gains against domestic data-sovereignty and privacy-regulation concerns that have driven protectionist rules elsewhere in the region.

word.definition: Deceitful in speech or conduct; deliberately saying or promising one thing while intending or doing another.
word.etymology: From Latin duplex/duplicis ("twofold, double"), via Anglo-Norman French duplicité ("doubleness, deceit"); the sense narrowed from merely "having two parts or aspects" to "deceitfully double-dealing" by the late 19th century.
word.example: Trump branded Iran's leadership "extremely duplicitous" Monday, after Tehran said talks with Oman on a temporary Hormuz shipping route were in their final stage while denying that any direct negotiations with Washington were under way at all.
